mathgap.title: Sequential processing of transfers
mathgap.principle: When a transfer statement appears, immediately adjust both the giver's and receiver's counts before processing any later statements, because subsequent statements refer to the updated counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement of the form "X gives K items to Y" is encountered.
mathgap.example: Processing all transfers after solving equations, thus using outdated counts for later statements.

mathgap.title: Signed difference equality
mathgap.principle: Translate statements of the form "the number of items that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of items that C and D have" into the equation (A - B) = (C - D), preserving the order and sign of each difference.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a comparison‑transfer statement that equates two signed differences.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "A has more than B" as |A - B| = C - D, ignoring the sign of the difference.

mathgap.title: Direct count assignment at point of mention
mathgap.principle: When a statement directly gives a count (e.g., "X has N items"), set X's current count to N at that point in the sequence; later transfers may modify it.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a plain count statement appears.
mathgap.example: Treating a "X has N items" statement as a permanent final count and never updating it after later transfers.

mathgap.title: Update both parties in a transfer
mathgap.principle: For a transfer "X gives K items to Y", subtract K from X's current count and add K to Y's current count.
mathgap.example: Only adding K to the receiver without subtracting K from the giver.

mathgap.title: Accumulate net change for multiple transfers
mathgap.principle: After processing all transfers, you can sum each person's gains and losses to compute their net change, which simplifies the final tally.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After all transfer statements have been applied, when you need the final counts.
mathgap.example: Summing net gains and losses while ignoring the order of transfers that affect intermediate constraints.

mathgap.title: Systematic linear solving
mathgap.principle: Translate all constraints into linear equations and solve the resulting system using substitution or elimination to obtain the unknown counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When you have a set of equations linking several variables.
mathgap.example: Guessing values or using ad‑hoc arithmetic instead of solving the linear system.

mathgap.title: Non‑negative integer check
mathgap.principle: All derived counts must be non‑negative integers; if any equation yields a negative or fractional value, the solution is invalid.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After solving for a variable, before accepting the result.
mathgap.example: Accepting a fractional or negative count as a valid answer.

mathgap.title: Multiplicative update handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says a person's count "increases by K times" (or is multiplied by a factor), multiply the current count accordingly rather than adding.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering multiplicative updates such as "doubles" or "triples".
mathgap.example: Treating a multiplication as an addition (e.g., interpreting "doubles" as "adds the same amount").

mathgap.title: Split operation handling
mathgap.principle: When a person splits all their items equally among two recipients, set the giver's count to zero and give each recipient half of the original amount.
mathgap.example: Leaving the giver with the original amount after a split instead of distributing it and zeroing the giver.

mathgap.title: Simple comparative statements handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says "X has N more (or fewer) items than Y", interpret it as a signed difference: set X = Y + N (or X = Y - N), preserving the direction as stated; do not reverse the relationship or treat it as an absolute difference.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a comparative statement of the form "X has N more/fewer items than Y" appears.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "X has 9 more potatoes than Y" as Y = X + 9 (reversed) or as |X - Y| = 9.

mathgap.description: Treating signed difference statements as absolute differences
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model often drops the sign and interprets "has more than" as a magnitude, leading to equations like |A - B| = C - D.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Translate such statements into signed differences preserving order: (A - B) = (C - D).

mathgap.description: Ignoring the sequential order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may aggregate transfers or apply them after solving equations, forgetting that later statements refer to updated counts.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process each transfer immediately when encountered, updating both parties before any subsequent statements.

mathgap.description: Assuming explicit counts are final after all transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats "X has N items" as a permanent value, not realizing later transfers can change it.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat explicit counts as the current count at that point; allow later transfers to modify them.

mathgap.description: Updating only the receiver in a transfer
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model forgets to subtract the transferred amount from the giver.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When processing a transfer, subtract the amount from the giver and add it to the receiver.

mathgap.description: Reversing the direction in "X has N more than Y" statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model misinterprets the comparative direction, swapping X and Y.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Maintain the order: X = Y + N (or X = Y - N) exactly as stated.
